summary:
GlacierWatch is an open-source interactive web app that helps scientists and researchers detect surface changes and warning signs at glacial lakes in Kyrgyzstan’s Tien Shan mountains. The region is prone to glacial lake outburst floods (GLOFs), and monitoring there is sparse and not transparent. The app uses NASA-ISRO NISAR radar data as its primary source. Sentinel-2 optical imagery, and NASA HLS and OPERA products supplement and validate it. Radar works day and night and through clouds, so it gives consistent observations in high mountains.

Users select a lake, choose a year or compare two dates and see before-and-after imagery with numeric change indicators. They judge for themselves whether there is a potential threat. The MVP shows three verified lakes. GlacierWatch turns complex radar observations into clear, accessible insight on a real climate hazard that affects local communities.
details:
GlacierWatch is an open-source, interactive satellite monitoring platform designed to help researchers and environmental monitoring specialists understand changes in glacial lakes across Kyrgyzstan.

How it works

GlacierWatch combines NASA–ISRO NISAR radar observations with Copernicus Sentinel-2 optical imagery. Users can select a lake, compare satellite observations from different dates using an interactive image slider, visualize water boundaries, and examine quantitative changes in lake surface area.

Our platform includes Petrov Lake, Ala-Kol Lake, and a glacial lake in the Batken region.

Scientific findings

Using NISAR L2 GCOV data, we measured Petrov Lake's open-water area at 4.53 km² in August 2026 and 4.47 km² in September 2026. The estimated difference remains within the method's sensitivity range. Sentinel-2 observations provided additional cross-sensor verification.

We also identified a 42.2% decrease in the open-water area of a glacial lake in Batken between September 4 and September 14, 2024, suggesting possible partial drainage.

Benefits and intended impact

Glacial lake outburst floods pose significant challenges to mountain communities, infrastructure, and water resources. GlacierWatch makes complex satellite observations more accessible, helping researchers identify changes that warrant further investigation and supporting more informed environmental monitoring.

Technology

We developed the project using:

  • NASA–ISRO NISAR L2 GCOV
  • NASA Earthdata, ASF and NASA Harmony
  • Copernicus Sentinel-2 Level-2A
  • Python, NumPy, Rasterio, SciPy and Shapely
  • HTML, CSS and JavaScript
  • GitHub and ChatGPT Sites
  • OpenAI Codex for development, research and testing

Creativity and scientific considerations

Our approach combines radar and optical observations within a transparent, user-friendly visual comparison tool. Every measurement is linked to its original satellite data, acquisition date and quality information.

We considered cloud contamination, snow and ice, radar shadow, seasonal differences, spatial resolution, data availability and measurement uncertainty.

Rather than making unsupported predictions, GlacierWatch empowers users to explore real scientific evidence and draw informed conclusions. Our long-term vision is to expand this accessible monitoring approach to vulnerable glacial lakes across Central Asia and other mountainous regions worldwide.
